summary: Preinstall dropper: downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727KB payload on npm install
details: The package advertises itself as a React component library for mobile webviews but ships only a trivial stub as its main entry (dist/index.js re-exports ionicons/icons; dist/ExampleComponent.js renders the literal string 'This is an example component.'). The substantive behavior lives in a `preinstall` lifecycle script (setup.mjs) that runs automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs is obfuscated with hex-named identifiers and downloads the Bun runtime (v1.3.13) from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts the platform-specific `bun` binary to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against the sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) using string-array rotation obfuscation (dispatcher `WV8StW` shifting a numeric/string constant array `n7gIxM`), so its behavior is not statically resolvable. Executing an obfuscated 727KB author-controlled payload under a freshly-downloaded alternate runtime at install time constitutes arbitrary code execution on every installer's machine, with the alternate-runtime step deliberately bypassing Node-based static analysis on the payload. The stub-only advertised functionality combined with the install-time dropper is consistent with a scope-squat impersonating the legitimate @servicetitan organization.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
